summary: Static code review + build verification of the iteration_2 HIGH fix (Supabase native invite PKCE callback). All checks pass: tsc --noEmit = 0 errors; next build succeeds with both /auth/callback AND /auth/confirm listed as dynamic (ƒ) routes. The end-to-end flow is logically correct: inviteUserByEmail(redirectTo=`${appUrl}/auth/callback?next=%2Finvite%2F<token>`) → Supabase /auth/v1/verify → our /auth/callback exchanges the ?code for a session (cookies set) → redirects to /invite/<token> → InvitePage useEffect sees authenticated user → mode='authed-set-password'. Middleware PUBLIC_PATHS already whitelists '/auth' so /auth/callback is publicly reachable. The .catch fallback on invite page correctly degrades to 'needs-password' on getUser throw. No regression detected on /login, /signup, /team, ClientForm copy-link UI.

minor.issue: safeNext sanitization only checks startsWith('/'). A protocol-relative URL like '//evil.com/path' would pass this check and could allow open redirect via `${origin}//evil.com/path`. Harden with: `next.startsWith('/') && !next.startsWith('//')`.
When error_description param is present, we redirect to /login without first attempting the code exchange. Fine, but we silently drop a potentially-still-valid `code`. Low risk.

On .catch fallback we silently drop the error — user sees needs-password with no indication their session failed. Could setError('Impossible de vérifier la session, créez un mot de passe.') to improve UX, but not blocking.

action_items: LOW (optional hardening): tighten safeNext in /auth/callback/route.ts to reject protocol-relative URLs (`!next.startsWith('//')`) to close a theoretical open-redirect vector.
LOW (UX polish): expose the catch-branch error on invite page (toast / setError) rather than silently falling back.
critical_code_review_comments: iteration_2 HIGH issue is RESOLVED. The new /app/fido/app/auth/callback/route.ts correctly exchanges the PKCE ?code via supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code), writes cookies via the server client, and 302s to the sanitized `next`. This makes mode='authed-set-password' actually reachable from a vanilla Supabase project.

invitations.ts L63 redirectTo uses encodeURIComponent(params.nextRedirect) so the inner slash of '/invite/<token>' is encoded to %2F — Supabase will NOT truncate the path, and our callback handler will decode it correctly via URLSearchParams. Verified mentally with a URL round-trip. ✓
Middleware PUBLIC_PATHS includes '/auth' and isPublic uses startsWith(p + '/') so '/auth/callback' resolves as public without the inner redirect loop. ✓
invite page .catch(() => setMode('needs-password')) handles the described edge case (network / malformed cookie) so the UI no longer stuck in 'checking' indefinitely.

Both /auth/callback and /auth/confirm remain available: /auth/confirm handles the token_hash+verifyOtp email template variant; /auth/callback handles the PKCE code variant (default Supabase invite). This is a sensible belt-and-suspenders setup.

No business-logic regressions observed in createInvitationInternal (copy-link inviteUrl built independently of the email channel), /login signUp, /team staff invites or ClientForm fallback copy-link UI.
No files >700 lines; invitations.ts = 192 lines, callback route = 42 lines. Clean, focused modules.
No MongoDB usage — ObjectId rule N/A. No hardcoded URLs — appUrl() reads NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.

success_rate.backend: 100% static+build; HIGH iteration_2 issue confirmed fixed

context_for_next_testing_agent: Next.js 15 + Supabase project at /app/fido. tsc=0 errors, next build=19 routes incl. /auth/callback (ƒ) and /auth/confirm (ƒ). The iteration_2 HIGH callback-url mismatch is resolved via the new /auth/callback route + redirectTo rewiring in sendInvitationEmail. No live Supabase available for e2e runtime verification; main agent / human should run one real invite through a Supabase staging project to confirm cookie-session establishment end-to-end, but the static logic is correct.
rca of the issue: N/A — iteration_2's RCA (Supabase default invite template routes via PKCE ?code and nothing in our codebase was exchanging that code) is addressed by: (1) adding /auth/callback that calls supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code), (2) pointing invitation redirectTo through /auth/callback?next=%2Finvite%2F<token>, (3) /auth already whitelisted in middleware PUBLIC_PATHS, (4) invite page .catch fallback for the degraded path.
